title: Jazzy Dutch Rice Pilaf
description: A resinous, aerated pilaf dish made with Arabic rice, poached to perfection in a halal-friendly broth. Perfect for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken broth, cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the Arabic rice and stir to coat with the broth. Cook for 5 minutes, or until the rice is lightly toasted.
Add 250ml of water and bring to a boil. Cover the saucepan with a tight-fitting lid and transfer to the oven.
Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes, or until the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender.
While the rice is cooking, mix the pomegranate molasses, lemon juice, and chopped scallions in a small bowl. Stir to combine.
To serve, fluff the rice with a fork and stir in the pomegranate molasses mixture, pine nuts, chopped parsley, crumbled sumac, and chopped cilantro.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds and serve warm.
Let the pilaf rest for 10 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.
Serve hot, garnished with additional sumac and pine nuts if desired.
